A Bloomberg report yesterday suggested the Apple Watch line could see quite significant changes in the future.

The report specifically noted that the company is exploring the possibility of launching one or more models with a round face design rather than a square one…

Most smartwatches are round

While square-faced watches have existed for well over a century, the vast majority of traditional watches are round, and the same goes for Android smartwatches. Examples include:

  • Amazfit Active Max
  • Samsung Galaxy Watch 9
  • Motorola Moto Watch
  • All Garmin models (Venu, Epix Pro, Forerunner, Fenix)
  • Google Pixel Watch

Apple's choice of a rectangular design has been something of an outlier, so it would be no surprise for the company to consider launching a round Apple Watch alongside it in the future.

The case for a round Apple Watch

The original reason Apple chose a rectangular design was that this format can display more information. The other screens we use daily — phones, tablets, laptops, monitors, and so on — are all rectangular, which is no coincidence.

Ultimately, the choice comes down to aesthetics versus utility. There will always be those who prioritise utility, so there's no doubt the rectangular Apple Watch design won't disappear. But there are also those who care greatly about appearance, and many people have a strong preference for round watches (whether traditional or smart).

Furthermore, not every Apple Watch user needs to display large amounts of information on the screen. Even if you don't check the screen often, there are plenty of good reasons to wear an Apple Watch. For example:

  • Health and fitness monitoring
  • Sleep tracking
  • Emergency features such as fall detection
  • Contactless payment

Of all the above, health and fitness monitoring is the main draw for many people. If you're not primarily using your Apple Watch as a content-consumption device, then a round screen could work just fine for you.

But the case for an Apple ring is even stronger

However, if you're this kind of user — someone who primarily uses an Apple Watch for health and fitness monitoring and really doesn't use it much for checking information — then I would argue a smart ring is a more… sensible choice.

I personally switched from an Apple Watch to an Oura smart ring in 2024, and have since upgraded to the fifth-generation model. I love how incredibly low-profile it is, how it lets me keep wearing the traditional watches I like, and how it only needs charging once a week.

Almost two years ago, I said I was very interested in smart rings as an Apple Watch alternative, and argued that Apple should launch such a product. I still firmly believe that today, and Gurman notes that Eddy Cue is also a smart ring fan, which makes the prospect of such a product launching quite high.

I do think it's possible Apple will launch a round Apple Watch model, but I think what we're more likely to see is an Apple ring. What do you think? Feel free to share your views in the comments.
